0.0.n: This borrowed word usually refers to male salaried company employees.

0.1.n: Marks サラリーマン as the people who say this.

0.2.n: Describes how frequently office workers say this, rather than how well they say it.

0.3.n: 言う is plain present; casual じゃん invites agreement, like reminding someone of something familiar.

0.5.n: Combines with 終わり to describe the end of the working day.

0.6.n: A noun from 終わる, used in 仕事終わり to mean finishing work.

0.7.n: Marks 仕事終わり as the time when the outing happens.

0.8.n: An 居酒屋 serves alcoholic drinks alongside food, often shared in small dishes.

0.9.n: Marks 居酒屋 as the destination of 行って.

0.10.n: The て-form of 行く links going to the pub with drinking there.

0.11.n: Plain present form directly describes 生ビール: the beer that someone drinks.

0.12.n: 生 here distinguishes beer served on tap, a common order at an izakaya.

0.13.n: Marks the beer described by the preceding actions as what is being praised.

0.14.n: Expresses an enthusiastic judgment; casual speech leaves out だ here.

0.15.n: Casually marks the preceding statement as the content of what office workers say.

1.0.n: This is the opening sound of one drawn-out response, not a separate word here.

1.1.n: Continues the same response; ー shows that the vowel sound is held longer.

2.0.n: Points back to the feeling about enjoying beer after work.

2.1.n: What the speaker is beginning to understand; casual speech leaves its marking particle unspoken.

2.2.n: Softens the statement by limiting how much the speaker understands.

2.3.n: 分かる in the て-form plus きた shows understanding developing up to now, not physical movement.

3.0.n: An informal response expressing interest or mild surprise; ー lengthens the final vowel.

0.lit: Office workers often say, you know: draft beer drunk after going to a pub at work’s end is the best.
0.tip: The quote comes after 言う, with final って linking it back to what people say.

1.tip: Although split into two tappable pieces, ああー is one drawn-out acknowledgment.

2.lit: That feeling, I have come to understand a little.
2.tip: てきた describes a change developing up to now: the speaker is beginning to understand.

3.tip: へえー signals interested surprise rather than simply agreeing.
